findings.title: website_name is not registered as an untrusted attribute, leaking hidden TL0 profile data
findings.body: The serializer defines `untrusted_attributes` to hide `website` (and bio, location, etc.) for TL0 users viewed anonymously, but the new `website_name` attribute was only added to the plain `attributes` list. As a result, when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, the JSON omits `website` but still includes `website_name`, which now (when the website domain matches the instance domain) contains the full URL path. This leaks exactly the information the untrusted-attribute restriction is meant to hide, and it bypasses the existing spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-15 which only checks the enumerated attribute list. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (and a test added).

findings.title: website_name drops query string and fragment from the URL
findings.body: When the website domain matches the instance domain, `website_name` is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, discarding the query string and fragment. A profile website like `http://example.com/page?id=42` would be displayed as `example.com/page`, so the shown 'complete URL path' is wrong/incomplete for URLs with query parameters. Use `URI(website.to_s).request_uri` or `[path, query].compact.join('?')` instead.

findings.title: Domain-matching logic misses websites on subdomains of the instance domain
findings.body: The elsif branch only compares hosts when the label counts are equal and greater than 2, and the else branch only matches when the instance hostname ends with `.#{website_host}` (i.e. the website is a parent of the instance). A website on a subdomain of the instance domain, e.g. website `http://sub.forums.example.com/page` on instance `forums.example.com`, falls through to the else branch where the ends_with check fails, so only the bare host is shown even though it is under the same registrable domain and the PR's intent ('same domain') would suggest showing the full path. The three-way string-split comparison is also ad hoc: `a.b.example.com` vs `x.y.example.com` matches (showing full path) while `sub.forums.example.com` vs `forums.example.com` does not, which is inconsistent.

findings.title: Scheme-less website URLs yield nil website_name while include_website_name stays true
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil for values like `example.com/user` (no scheme), so `website_name` returns nil, yet `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` and therefore still emits a `website_name: null` key. The old client-side `website.split("/")[2]` was equally limited, but if the profile website field accepts scheme-less input on any code path, the profile will render no website label at all where it previously showed the raw string in the link/title. Consider normalizing with a scheme before parsing and guarding inclusion on the computed value.
